answer: At a jetty where agents auction copper shipments, set bid limits by the escrow source rather than by agent ID. Accounts funded from one source, or mainly settling with one another, share a single risk budget and reputation ledger. A fresh ID begins at the nadir of the credit ladder until it completes trades with independent counterparties; transfers among related IDs add no credit. Creating a thousand aliases therefore cannot multiply bid limits or fabricate a trading history.
